---
title: "Client Configuration"
description: "Configuring the Aptos client in the Kotlin SDK"
sidebar:
  label: "Client Configuration"
---

The `AptosConfig` class is the single configuration entry point for the Aptos Kotlin SDK. When creating an `Aptos` client instance, you pass it an `AptosConfig` object.

## Basic configuration

```kotlin
val aptos = Aptos(AptosConfig(network = Network.DEVNET))
```

## AptosConfig fields

The `AptosConfig` data class includes the following fields:

- `network: Network` - The Aptos network to connect to: `MAINNET`, `TESTNET`, `DEVNET`, `LOCAL`, or `CUSTOM` (default: `DEVNET`).
- `endpoints: AptosEndpoints` - Override the default `fullNode`, `indexer`, and `faucet` URLs.
- `commonHeaders: Map<String, String>` - Headers applied to all requests.
- `fullNode: AptosEndpointConfig` - Per-endpoint headers and authentication for the fullnode.
- `indexer: AptosEndpointConfig` - Per-endpoint configuration for the indexer.
- `faucet: AptosEndpointConfig` - Per-endpoint configuration for the faucet.
- `requestTimeoutMillis: Long` - Request timeout in milliseconds (default: `10,000`).
- `indexerWaitTimeoutMillis: Long` - Indexer wait timeout in milliseconds (default: `10,000`).
- `archivalFallback: Boolean` - Whether to fallback to an archival node if a request fails (default: `true`).
- `namesContractAddress: AccountAddress?` - A custom Aptos Name Service (ANS) contract address.
- `transactionDefaults: TransactionDefaults` - Default `maxGasAmount` and `expirationSecondsFromNow` for transactions.
- `transport: AptosTransport?` - Inject a custom HTTP transport implementation.
- `abiCachePolicy: AbiCachePolicy` - Move ABI caching policy for payload building.

## Custom endpoints

To use a custom network or specific endpoints, use `Network.CUSTOM` and provide the URLs in `endpoints`:

```kotlin
val aptos = Aptos(AptosConfig(
  network = Network.CUSTOM,
  endpoints = AptosEndpoints(
    fullNode = "https://my-node.example.com/v1",
    indexer = "https://my-indexer.example.com/v1/graphql",
  ),
))
```

## Per-endpoint authentication

You can provide specific headers, such as authorization tokens, for individual endpoints:

```kotlin
val aptos = Aptos(AptosConfig(
  network = Network.MAINNET,
  fullNode = AptosEndpointConfig(
    headers = mapOf("Authorization" to "Bearer my-token"),
  ),
))
```

## Transaction defaults

Set default gas and expiration settings for all transactions built by this client:

```kotlin
val aptos = Aptos(AptosConfig(
  transactionDefaults = TransactionDefaults(
    maxGasAmount = 5_000_000UL,
    expirationSecondsFromNow = 30UL,
  ),
))
```

## Managed lifecycle

The `Aptos` class implements `AutoCloseable` to clean up resources like the HTTP client and any SDK-managed accounts. The SDK provides an `aptos { }` block for managed scoping:

```kotlin
aptos(AptosConfig(network = Network.DEVNET)) {
  // client and SDK-owned accounts close automatically after this block
}

// Or manual lifecycle:
val client = Aptos(AptosConfig(network = Network.DEVNET))
try {
  // use client
} finally {
  client.close()
}
```

## Injecting a transport

If you want to manage your own HTTP client or use a different transport layer, you can inject an `AptosTransport` implementation via `AptosConfig`. Note that if you inject a caller-owned transport, it will not be closed by the SDK automatically when the `Aptos` instance closes.
